name: Palmitoyl oligopeptide

lead: Palmitoyl oligopeptide is an ingredient-list term for short peptides attached to a fatty acid, used in anti-ageing creams.
No dedicated clinical trial was found.

paras: Formulators describe such peptides as promoting collagen synthesis; the fatty chain is intended to aid skin penetration.
No specific harms were found in the sources reviewed.

lead: Palmitoyl oligopeptide is a generic cosmetic-ingredient name for short peptides linked to palmitic acid, used in anti-ageing creams as collagen-promoting "signal" ingredients. Patent literature lists fatty-acid-grafted peptides, specifically C16 palmitoyl oligopeptides, among agents said to promote collagen synthesis [1].

Published evidence specific to the ingredient is limited. A 2015 methods study used imaging and histology to evaluate extracellular matrix and the epidermal-dermal junction, and examined effects of age and peptide applications [2].

paras: It appears as an ingredient in anti-ageing formulations and in sensitive-skin products that contain synthetic peptides [3][1].

No studies found isolating palmitoyl oligopeptide in a clinical trial. A 2015 study developed a multi-technique methodology (mass spectrometric imaging, confocal microscopy, echography, histology) to assess skin matrix changes with age and after peptide applications [2].
